findings.description: The Lambda function's environment variables contain a plaintext AWS access key and secret key. These are embedded directly in source-controlled Terraform code, making them visible to anyone with repo access and exposing them via the Lambda console/API, risking credential compromise.

No KMS key (kms_key_arn) is specified for the Lambda function, so environment variables (including the embedded secrets) are only protected by the default AWS-managed key rather than a customer-managed key, weakening encryption-at-rest controls for sensitive data.
The function uses nodejs12.x, which is an end-of-life/deprecated runtime no longer receiving security patches, increasing exposure to unpatched vulnerabilities.
